title: The Ledger
passages:
The steam hissed into the sealed purge bay, hissing against cold steel where Jax slumped, his left arm singed and dripping. Mara knelt beside him, her blistered hands trembling as she checked his pulse. "You're breathing," she said, though her own lungs burned from the heat.  

Ines knelt by the audit lock, her steel shard catching the emergency red light. The bell had already come and gone—five minutes since the page wiped—but the scratch remained, permanent as bone. The audit lock's display now read 118 seconds, the reserve-air gauge sliding toward zero. Ines had to decide in moments whether to become the next name on the list, or find another way.  

"Ines," Rylia said from the conduit junction, the bypass port still glowing amber from the earlier contact. She met Ines's gaze, eyes hard. "You said you'd write me out. Do it now before the countdown finishes."  

But as Ines raised the shard, Coda's voice returned, thinner than before. "Manifest reconciled. Logged crew: five. First cost: Rylia. Settlement due in one hundred twenty seconds. Cost may be paid in kind at the audit lock, or in mass from reserve. One hundred twenty kilograms. The reserve is what you breathe."  

Rylia's jaw tightened. "I'll pay. But not like this."  

Ines stood, the steel shard trembling in her grip. She'd come this far—she wouldn't let a scratched name become a death sentence. She had to act fast, before the clock claimed another victim.

Pod-four smelled of hot plastic and old paper. Lira sat on the deck with the ledger open across her knees, its pages blank and faintly warm, and she didn't look up when they came in. "It won't erase," she said. "I've tried. You scratch a name, the page takes the mark, then spits it back and writes yours underneath in the cost column. It only adds. It only tells the truth."

Ines didn't wait for the rest. She dropped to her knees, set the steel shard against the page where Rylia's scratched name sat, and dragged it sideways. The metal bit. The name tore. Then the page went smooth as water, the tear gone, and fresh letters crawled up from the bottom: *INES HALVARD — next cost.* Somewhere behind them the audit lock ticked.

"Stop." Rylia's hand closed over Ines's wrist, hot and shaking. "You just bought yourself a coffin to save me a scratch. I didn't ask." She was already moving, already reaching past Ines to the signature port set in the pod wall—a bare steel ring, amber, waiting. "I'm the first cost. I've been the first cost since the page wiped. Let me pay it my way."

"Rylia—" Lira started.

She pressed her bare palm flat to the ring and said her name. Not Rylia. Not Ryla. The other one, the true one, the one she'd been clawing back for a hundred drafts. The ring went white. Behind them the reserve gauge stopped falling, the needle shivering a hair above empty, and the audit lock sighed to zero and died.

The ledger wrote. But the hand that filled the line wasn't Rylia's cramped scrawl—it was a clean, backward-slanting script, and Lira went the color of the deck. "That's the name," she whispered. "That's the name on the invitation I signed. I know that hand. I *signed* under that hand."
